value: This article defines the placebo effect as a beneficial health outcome stemming from a patient's anticipation of benefit or positive interaction with a healthcare provider. It highlights the importance of randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trials as the "gold standard" for evaluating interventions, by comparing an experimental group to a control group receiving an inactive placebo. The text also summarizes NCCIH-supported research, revealing that placebo responses may have a genetic component, can occur unconsciously, and can even be effective when patients are aware they are receiving a placebo.
